samples.summary: `--round N` bypasses the self-review bound and silently discards the carry-forward, the exact hole closed for `--fresh`
samples.evidence: `const spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round;` (line 987) only corrects for the `--fresh` renumbering. When `--round` is supplied explicitly, `round = Number(args.round)` (line 979) is used verbatim as `spentRound`, so after three real rounds on disk `node spec-to-pr.mjs review --round 1` gives `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`, the refusal at line 989 never fires, and a fourth round runs presenting itself as a clean first one — the precise failure the block comment at lines 980-986 says the bound exists to prevent. It is worse than the `--fresh` case it was written against: `prior = round > 1 ? priorFindingsFor(base, round) : []` (line 1055) then carries nothing, and `mkdirSync(dir)` + the panel overwrite the existing `round-1/<lens>/verdict.json` files, destroying the verdicts a later round would have read back (`--fresh` at least only deletes after the bound has let the run through). `reviewArgsError` validates only that `--round` is a positive integer, and nothing else compares it against `nextRound(onDiskBefore)`. Suggested fix: `const spentRound = Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` for every path, not just `args.fresh`.

samples.summary: `priorFindingsFor`'s documented "never throws" contract is broken by the unguarded `readdirSync(base)` inside `roundsOnDisk`
samples.evidence: `roundsOnDisk` opens with `roundsIn(readdirSync(base))` (line 833) with no try/catch, while the per-round `readdirSync` immediately below IS guarded and its docblock (lines 822-831) explains the guard exists precisely so "`priorFindingsFor`'s 'never throws' contract" is not broken "from underneath". A missing, unreadable (EACCES) or non-directory `base` therefore throws out of `priorFindingsFor` (line 861) and out of `cmdReview`'s dry-run branch (line 1023) as an uncaught ENOENT/EACCES stack rather than the `fail()` sentence every other refusal on this path uses. In `cmdReview` the base was just created so it is normally present, but both functions are exported and documented as total, and the window between `mkdirSync`/`realpathSync` and the read is exactly the shared-/tmp race the surrounding guard is about. Wrapping line 833 in the same try/catch → `[]` matches the module's stated fail direction (carry fewer findings).
searchedFor: grep for roundsOnDisk/priorFindingsFor call sites across the repo (only spec-to-pr.mjs and its test)

samples.summary: `carryForwardFindings` spreads raw model objects through `mergedFrom`, contradicting its own "PROJECT, never spread" contract and drifting from the cloud projection
samples.evidence: Line 174 is `mergedFrom: Array.isArray(f.mergedFrom) ? f.mergedFrom : undefined` — the array is passed through by reference, so every key each nested object chose to write (including `infra`, `lane`, `file`, arbitrary chatter) reaches the next round's verifier prompt. The comment directly above (lines 160-165) states the rule is to project rather than spread "because a spread carries every key a lens chose to write — `infra` included", and the cloud copy this function is explicitly mirroring rebuilds each entry: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1028` maps `mergedFrom` to `{ severity: norm(m.severity), summary: trim(m.summary,500), adjudication: Number.isInteger(m.adjudication?.upheld) ? { upheld } : undefined }` and caps it at 5. `isInfraRecord` only inspects the top level, so a nested `infra: true` is not filtered either. Not a crash, but it is untrusted model output escaping the projection the function's contract promises, and the two carry-forward channels no longer agree on what a carried `mergedFrom` contains.

samples.summary: `pickLatestVerdicts` accumulates into a bare object, so a lens directory named `__proto__` is silently dropped
samples.evidence: `const out = {}` / `out[lens] = r` (lines 201, 210) — assigning to the key `__proto__` on a plain object sets the prototype instead of creating an own property, and the value being a number makes it a silent no-op, so `Object.entries(picks)` in `priorFindingsFor` (line 863) would never see that lens and its findings would stop carrying forward. Lens ids come from `lenses.json`, so this is only reachable via a junk directory in the predictable, shared temp base — contrived, but `Object.create(null)` (or a `Map`) removes it for free. The `seen` lookup at line 208 has the same inherited-property exposure (`seen["constructor"] !== undefined` is true) though it happens to behave correctly because the subsequent `>=` comparison is false.

finding.summary: `--round N` bypasses the self-review bound and silently discards the carry-forward, the exact hole closed for `--fresh`
finding.evidence: `const spentRound = args.fresh ? Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore)) : round;` (line 987) only corrects for the `--fresh` renumbering. When `--round` is supplied explicitly, `round = Number(args.round)` (line 979) is used verbatim as `spentRound`, so after three real rounds on disk `node spec-to-pr.mjs review --round 1` gives `roundBoundNotice(1) === ""`, the refusal at line 989 never fires, and a fourth round runs presenting itself as a clean first one — the precise failure the block comment at lines 980-986 says the bound exists to prevent. verdict.reason: The code matches the finding verbatim. spec-to-pr.mjs:987 applies the `Math.max(round, nextRound(onDiskBefore))` correction only under `args.fresh`; an explicit `--round` (979) flows straight into `spentRound`, so `roundBoundNotice(spentRound)` (988, definition at 229) returns "" for `--round 1` and the refusal at 989-996 never fires after three real rounds — defeating the invariant the comment at 980-986 and the docstring at 216-236 state (`--force` as the only door). The consequences are real too: `prior` is empty for round 1 (1055) so the carry-forward is silently dropped, and `mkdirSync(dir)` (1041) with the panel's `--out outDir` (1047) rewrites the existing `round-1/<lens>/verdict.json` that `roundsOnDisk` (832) and `pickLatestVerdicts` (200) read back. The only validation of `--round` is `reviewArgsError` (605-613), which checks positive-integer-ness and nothing about rounds already on disk; no other guard in `cmdReview` (900-966) compares them. `--round N` is a documented flag (30, 1133), so the path is reachable in ordinary use. Broken invariant plus overwrite of state a later round depends on is in the correctness lane and blocking.
